package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware distributed via bundling/drive-by downloads, not a package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: Fireball is a large-scale browser hijacker and ad fraud malware that infects millions of systems worldwide. It forcibly modifies browser settings, injects unauthorized advertisements, and enables remote code execution, allowing attackers to control infected machines, monetize via ad fraud, and potentially escalate to full system compromise.

execution_context.trigger: At system startup or browser launch
execution_context.file_location: Injected into the browser process memory or installed as a browser extension/add-on (e.g., Chrome/Firefox extension directory, or as a DLL in browser process space)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At system startup or browser launch, the code forcibly sets the browser homepage and default search engine to attacker-controlled domains, injects unauthorized advertisements into web pages, and checks for remote commands from a C2 server, enabling browser hijacking, ad fraud, and remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code performs unauthorized modification of browser configuration, injects ads into user web sessions, and includes a mechanism to receive and execute remote commands, all without user consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate browser extensions or software should not alter user browser settings, inject ads, or execute remote code without explicit user or administrator approval.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise browser management tools may set homepage or search engine, but only with user/admin consent and never with ad injection or arbitrary remote code execution capabilities.
key_indicators: Unauthorized changes to browser homepage and search engine settings
Injection of advertisements into web pages outside of normal ad networks
Presence of remote command-and-control logic enabling arbitrary code execution
Modification of browser configuration files or registry entries
Installation of unknown or suspicious browser extensions/add-ons

attack_chain.action: Malware is delivered to the victim's machine via software bundling or drive-by download, often masquerading as legitimate software.
attack_chain.leads_to: Installation and persistence of the Fireball malware on the system

attack_chain.action: On system startup or browser launch, the malware executes and hijacks browser settings, injects unauthorized ads, and establishes remote control capabilities.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ongoing ad fraud, browser hijacking, and establishment of a remote command channel

attack_chain.action: Malware receives and executes remote commands from the attacker's C2 infrastructure, potentially downloading additional payloads or exfiltrating data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full compromise of the system, further monetization, or lateral movement

behavioral_signatures: Unauthorized modification of browser homepage and search engine settings to non-default, attacker-controlled domains
Injection of advertisements into web pages outside of legitimate ad networks
Browser extension or process making outbound requests to known Fireball C2 or ad fraud domains
Unexpected execution of code within the browser process or extension context
file_indicators: Presence of unknown or suspicious browser extensions/add-ons in extension directories
Unexpected changes to browser configuration files (e.g., prefs.js for Firefox, registry keys for IE/Edge/Chrome)
Files or processes with names mimicking legitimate browser components but located in non-standard directories
Persistence mechanisms such as scheduled tasks or registry run keys referencing suspicious binaries
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known Fireball C2 domains or ad fraud infrastructure (e.g., malicious-search.com)
Frequent HTTP requests from browser processes to domains set as new homepage or search engine
Unusual traffic patterns or POST requests from browser extensions to external servers
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unauthorized changes to browser settings and configuration files, unexpected or suspicious browser extensions, and outbound network connections to known Fireball C2 or ad fraud domains. Correlate browser configuration changes with process creation and network activity. Use endpoint protection to detect browser hijacking behaviors, ad injection, and remote code execution attempts. Investigate persistence mechanisms such as scheduled tasks or registry run keys referencing unknown binaries.
